title: Exciton switching and tunable exciton-phonon coupling in Oxygen doped ZnO nanorods
authors: Aiswarya Rath, Kalyan Ghosh, Pratap K Sahoo
abstract: Self ion doping in ZnO nanorods offers a powerful route to dynamically control excitonic states and light matter interactions. Here, vertically aligned hexagonal ZnO nanorods were irradiated with 250 keV oxygen ions to establish a direct link between irradiation induced defects and excitonic and optical responses. Increasing ion fluence progressively quenches the near band edge emission at 380 nm, leading to a complete exciton OFF state, while thermal annealing restores the emission, yielding a reversible exciton OFF or ON response. This switching originates from defect mediated modification and thermal recovery of excitonic states. The defect band emission, between 400 to 750 nm, exhibits quasi periodic whispering gallery mode like resonances that are progressively suppressed as irradiation alters nanorod geometry and optical confinement. Low-temperature photoluminescence resolves D0X, FX 1LO, and FX 2LO transitions, whose temperature evolution follows the Bose Einstein model. The non-monotonic variation of excition phonon coupling strength reveals a competition among irradiation induced defects, lattice distortion, and exciton localization in determining exciton phonon coupling. These results establish Oxygen ion irradiation as a means to simultaneously engineer excitonic switching, exciton phonon interactions, and optical resonances, providing a pathway toward defect programmable ZnO nanophotonic and optoelectronic devices.
summary: This work demonstrates that oxygen ion irradiation can be used to engineer ZnO nanorods, achieving a reversible 'switching' of excitonic emission. By analyzing the temperature-dependent photoluminescence, the researchers quantified how the ion damage systematically tunes the exciton-phonon coupling strength, paving the way for defect-programmable nanophotonic devices.
main_problem: The study aims to dynamically control excitonic states and light-matter interactions in ZnO nanorods by engineering defects using oxygen ion irradiation.
main_result: Oxygen ion irradiation enables a reversible exciton OFF/ON switching mechanism and allows for the systematic tuning of the exciton-phonon coupling strength.
method: The research combines ion implantation (250 keV O+ irradiation) with structural characterization (FESEM, XRD) and detailed optical spectroscopy (PL, temperature-dependent PL) analyzed using the Bose-Einstein model.
model_or_system: The physical system is vertically aligned hexagonal ZnO nanorods. The analysis models exciton-phonon coupling using the Bose-Einstein model, while structural changes are tracked via ion implantation depth profiles and crystal structure analysis.

figures_summary: Figures illustrate the depth profiles of implanted ions and structural disorder (XRD), while PL spectra show the quenching of NBE emission and the temperature evolution of exciton transitions.
paper_structure: The paper follows a progression from establishing the physical system and methodology (ion implantation, structural analysis) to demonstrating the primary phenomenon (exciton switching) and finally quantifying the underlying physics (tunable exciton-phonon coupling via Bose-Einstein fitting).
why_interesting: The ability to use controlled ion irradiation to engineer specific electronic states (exciton switching) and tune fundamental coupling constants ($a_{	ext{BE}}$) in a solid-state semiconductor is highly relevant for designing quantum emitters and optoelectronic devices.
